title: Contraction Families
goal: I can make contractions like I'm, they're, she's, I'll and we've.

card.desc: Bristol practices the contraction families for I, you, he, she, it, we and they: I'm; you're, we're, they're; he's, she's, it's; I'll, you'll, we'll; I've, we've, they've. She builds them with word cards, learns to look after the apostrophe to find the hiding word, and fixes apostrophes in the wrong spot (did'nt → didn't).

win: Great job! You know all the contraction families!

slides.title: Contraction Families: On Your Own
slides.text: You met the contraction families with Jonathan. Now practice on your own! ✏️

slides.title: The families
slides.text: The apostrophe takes the place of the missing letters.

steps.text: will: I'll, you'll, we'll · have: I've, we've, they've

slides.tip: Look after the apostrophe: s → is, re → are, ll → will, ve → have.

slides.title: Say it out loud
slides.text: Say these out loud. You can tell your mom!
prompts: Say we are, I will and they have as contractions.
Which two letters drop out of will?
Tell your mom a sentence with she's.

slides.title: Make the contraction
slides.text: Type the contraction. Put the apostrophe in the right spot.

items.why: They are → They're. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.
items.no: Push They are together. Take out the a. Put in an apostrophe.

items.why: I will → I'll. The apostrophe takes the place of the w and i.
items.no: Push I will together. Take out the w and i. Put in an apostrophe.

items.why: He is → He's. The apostrophe takes the place of the i.
items.no: Push He is together. Take out the i. Put in an apostrophe.
Look after the apostrophe: ll. Which word ends with ll?
Look after the apostrophe: re. Which word ends with re?
Look after the apostrophe: ve. Which word ends with ve?

slides.title: Which word is hiding?
slides.text: Tap a word. Then tap the box with the word that made it.

items.hint: Only an m is after the apostrophe.
Only an s is after the apostrophe.
Only an s is after the apostrophe.

items.q: Ellie wrote is'nt. What is the right way?
items.why: The o was between n and t: isn't.
no: The apostrophe does not go at the end.
The o dropped out between n and t. Put the apostrophe there.

items.q: Liz wrote theyr'e. What is the right way?
items.why: The a drops out right after they: they're.
no: A contraction needs an apostrophe.
The a was right after they. The apostrophe goes there.

items.q: Mom is in the kitchen. ____ making soup.
items.why: Mom is a she. She is → She's making soup.
no: He's is for a boy or a man.
She'll means she will. She will making soup does not make sense.

items.q: My brothers are outside. ____ playing ball.
no: We're means we are. The story is about my brothers, so use they.
They've means they have. They have playing does not make sense.

items.q: Ellie had 52 cards. She gave away 25. How many are left?
items.why: She gave some away, so subtract. 52 − 25 = 27. Check: 27 + 25 = 52.
items.no: Cards went away. Subtract. Then add back to check.
items.hint: Regroup a ten: 12 − 5 in the ones.

sets.q: Tap the word with the apostrophe in the right spot.
sets.why: The a drops out right after they: they're.
no: The a in are drops out. Only re stays.
they stays whole. The apostrophe goes after they.

sets.q: Mom says, "____ proud of you!" (I am)
no: I'll means I will.
I've means I have.
we're means we are.
we'll means we will.

sets.why: They are → They're. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.
sets.no: Push They are together. Take out the a. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.why: We have → We've. The apostrophe takes the place of the h and a.
sets.no: Push We have together. Take out the h and a. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.why: It is → It's. The apostrophe takes the place of the i.
sets.no: Push It is together. Take out the i. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.q: Tap the right way to write I will.
sets.why: The w and i drop out: I'll.
no: Ill with no apostrophe means sick. A contraction needs an apostrophe.
Two l's stay together after the apostrophe: 'll.
He's means he is.
She'll means she will.
Your shows something belongs to you, like your coat.
You'll means you will.

sets.why: I am → I'm. The apostrophe takes the place of the a.
sets.no: Push I am together. Take out the a. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.why: We will → We'll. The apostrophe takes the place of the w and i.
sets.no: Push We will together. Take out the w and i. Put in an apostrophe.

sets.q: ____ the tallest boy in my class. (He is)
sets.why: He is → He's. The apostrophe takes the place of the i.
sets.no: Push He is together. Take out the i. Put in an apostrophe.
re is after the apostrophe. Which word ends with re?

sets.q: Find the word that means we are.
no: were is a different word, like we were at home. It has no apostrophe.
Only the a drops out. The e stays: we're.

sets.q: The dogs are hungry. ____ barking. (They are)
no: They've means they have.
They'll means they will.
she's means she is.
we'll means we will.

practice.intro: Three tries on each one. Only your first try counts. Look after the apostrophe to find the hiding word.

questions.q: Ellie wrote did'nt. What is the right way?

no: The o dropped out between n and t. Put the apostrophe there.
A contraction needs an apostrophe where the letter dropped out.
I'm means I am.

questions.q: ____ cold today. Wear a coat! (It is)
no: I'm means I am.
It'll means it will.

questions.q: Which contraction is missing the letters w and i?
questions.why: we will → we'll. The w and i drop out.
no: we're is missing the a from are.
we've is missing the h and a from have.

questions.why: You are my friend → You're my friend.
no: Your shows something belongs to you. You need you are → you're.
The apostrophe does not go at the end.

teacher.objective: Bristol makes and takes apart the pronoun contraction families: I'm; you're, we're, they're; he's, she's, it's; I'll, you'll, we'll; I've, we've, they've. She learns to look after the apostrophe to find the hiding word (s → is, re → are, ll → will, ve → have) and fixes apostrophes in the wrong spot (did'nt → didn't). Week 6 Day 2 (Practice it).
materials: The Class lesson open on your laptop (course page, code 9110)
12 index cards, one word on each: I, you, he, she, it, we, they, am, are, is, will, have
Sticky notes (she draws an apostrophe on them)
Printed packet (2 pages) to send home

plan.do: Class slide 1. What is a contraction? What does the apostrophe do?
Class slide 2. Her n't word from the book, and a sentence with I, he, she or they.
Class slide 3. Check Monday's After-Class score first.
Class slide 4. She lays out the 7 pronoun cards.
Class slides 5–7. She builds I'm, they're and she's with cards and sticky notes.
Class slides 8–9. Two letters drop out of each.
Class slide 10. She builds they're, I'll, we've and writes each on the whiteboard.
Class slide 11. Look after the apostrophe: s, re, ll.
Class slides 12–13. Whiteboard first, then she types.
Class slides 14–15. She writes the wrong word, fixes it, then picks.
Class slide 16. She reads each sentence with her choice.
Class slide 17. You write; she catches your apostrophe mistake.
Class slide 18. Show the task list: tonight and Wednesday are the big homework days.

watch: Keeping the dropped letter and adding an apostrophe (they'are, I'am). Ask: "Which letter drops out?"
Apostrophe in the wrong spot (the'yre, theyr'e, did'nt). Ask: "Where was the missing letter? Put it right there."
your for you're, and were for we're. Say the long way: "you are my friend" makes sense, so it's you're.
I'll written as Ill or I'l. Two l's stay; the apostrophe replaces w and i.
A lowercase i in I'm, I'll and I've. I is always a capital letter.
it's and its. If she asks: it's with an apostrophe is short for it is. Its with no apostrophe shows something belongs to it (we learn that later).
Typed answers ignore apostrophes, so check the spot on her whiteboard and in the packet.

packet_key.answer: Any sentence that uses I'm correctly (I'm = I am), with a capital letter and a period.
Any sentence that uses they're correctly (they're = they are), with a capital letter and a period. Not their or there.

slides.title: Contraction Families
slides.text:
Monday you met the not family.
Today you meet more families! 👨‍👩‍👧

notes.do: Before she arrives, write these on index cards, one word per card: I, you, he, she, it, we, they, am, are, is, will, have. Set out sticky notes, the whiteboard and her book.
notes.say: "Monday you learned the not family. Today you learn the families that go with I, you, he, she, it, we and they."
notes.ask: "What is a contraction? What does the apostrophe do?"
notes.listen: Two words pushed together; the apostrophe takes the place of the missing letters.

slides.title: Hunting in my book
slides.text: Think about the book you are reading.
prompts: What happened in your book since Monday?
Did you find an n't word? What two words make it?
Find a sentence that starts with I, he, she or they. Read it.

notes.do: About 6 minutes. She shows the page with her n't word.
notes.ask: "What two words make it?" "Who is he or she in that sentence?"
notes.listen: The two words are right (didn't = did not). She can tell who the he or she is. Say: "Words like he and she can push together too. Let's see how."

items.why: can not → can't. The n and o drop out.
no: Only one n is left. The n and o of not drop out.
can stays whole. The apostrophe goes after can.

items.q: We ____ go to the park yesterday. (did not)
items.why: did not → didn't. The o drops out.
items.no: Take out the o in not. Put in an apostrophe.

notes.do: Check Monday's After-Class score first. She spells didn't out loud before she types it.
notes.ask: "Where does the apostrophe go in didn't?"
notes.listen: can't; d-i-d-n-apostrophe-t. If she is shaky, redo one paper strip from Monday.

slides.title: Words for people
slides.text: These words take the place of a name.

visual.text: I · you · he · she · it · we · they

steps.text: These words push together with am, are, is, will and have.

notes.do: She reads the 7 words out loud, then lays out the 7 word cards (I, you, he, she, it, we, they) in a row.
notes.ask: "Liz and Ellie went home. Which word can take the place of Liz and Ellie?"

slides.title: I am → I'm
slides.tip: I'm always starts with a capital I.

notes.do: She puts the I card next to the am card and covers the a with a sticky note. She draws the apostrophe on the sticky note.

slides.title: The are family
slides.tip: The re stays. Only the a drops out.

notes.do: Reveal one at a time. She builds they're with the cards and a sticky note.
notes.ask: "In they're, which letters are after the apostrophe?"
notes.listen: "r and e." Watch for theyr'e or the'yre.

slides.title: The is family
slides.tip: Only the s is left after the apostrophe.

notes.do: Reveal one at a time. She builds she's with the cards.
notes.listen: "It is." If she asks about its with no apostrophe, say: "That is a different word. It shows something belongs to it. Today, it's with an apostrophe means it is."

notes.do: She covers w and i with one sticky note.
notes.ask: "How many letters did you cover? How many l's are left?"
notes.listen: Two letters (w, i); two l's. Without the apostrophe, I'll looks like ill (sick). That is why the apostrophe matters.

notes.do: She covers h and a with one sticky note.
notes.listen: h and a. The v and e stay.

slides.title: Card families
slides.text: Use your word cards and sticky notes.
prompts: Make they're. Which letter did you cover?
Make I'll. How many letters did you cover?
Make we've. Which letters did you cover?

notes.do: About 7 minutes. She builds each one with a pronoun card, a word card and a sticky note with an apostrophe drawn on it. Then she writes each contraction on the whiteboard.
notes.ask: After each one: "Read it. Now say the two long words."
notes.listen: they're (a); I'll (2: w and i); we've (h and a). On the whiteboard, check the apostrophe spot on every word.

slides.title: Which word is hiding?
slides.text: What word made each contraction? Tap a word. Then tap the box.

items.hint: re is after the apostrophe. Which word ends with re?
Only an s is after the apostrophe. Which word ends with s?
Only an s is after the apostrophe.
ll is after the apostrophe. Which word ends with ll?
Only an s is after the apostrophe.

slides.done: Look after the apostrophe: s → is, re → are, ll → will.

notes.say: "Here is a secret: look at the letters after the apostrophe."
notes.listen: s → is, re → are, ll → will.

items.no: Look after the apostrophe: re. Which word ends with re?
Look after the apostrophe: ve. Which word ends with ve?
Only an s is after the apostrophe.

items.why: we are → we're. The a drops out.
items.no: Take out the a in are. Put in an apostrophe.

items.why: I will → I'll. The w and i drop out.
items.no: Take out the w and i in will. Put in an apostrophe.

items.why: they have → they've. The h and a drop out.
items.no: Take out the h and a in have. Put in an apostrophe.

notes.do: She writes each one on the whiteboard first, then types it.
notes.listen: we're, I'll, they've. Typing ignores the apostrophe, so check the whiteboard for the spot.

slides.title: Right spot!
slides.text: Ask: which letters dropped out? The apostrophe goes right there.

steps.text:
did'nt ❌ → didn't ✅
The o was between n and t.

Ill ❌ → I'll ✅
Without the apostrophe, ill is a different word. It means sick!

slides.tip: First find the missing letters. Then put the apostrophe in their place.

notes.do: She writes the wrong word on the whiteboard, then fixes it under it.
notes.ask: "What letter dropped out of did not? Where was it?"
notes.listen: "The o, between the n and the t."

items.q: Pick the right way to write we have.
items.why: The h and a drop out: we've.
no: The h and a drop out. Only ve stays.
The apostrophe does not go at the end.

items.q: Pick the right way to write you are.
no: your shows something belongs to you, like your hat. you are → you're.
The apostrophe does not go at the end.

items.q: Pick the right way to write did not.
no: The o was between n and t. The apostrophe goes there.
A contraction needs an apostrophe.

notes.do: She says why each wrong one is wrong before she picks.
notes.listen: we've; you're (your means it belongs to you); didn't.

no: I'll means I will.
I've means I have.

items.q: Look at the cat. ____ sleeping. (It is)
no: It'll means it will.
I'm means I am.

items.q: ____ make a card for Dad. (We will)
no: We're means we are.
We've means we have.

notes.do: She reads each sentence out loud with her choice.

slides.title: Talk with contractions
prompts: Tell me one thing with I'm, one with I'll and one with I've.
Tell me about your family with they're.
Tell me about River or Cam with he's or she's.

notes.do: Quick and fun. You write each contraction she says on the whiteboard; she checks your apostrophe.
notes.listen: Each contraction fits her sentence. Make one apostrophe mistake on purpose and let her catch it.

slides.title: What did you learn?
prompts: What letters drop out of will? Of have?
